studies.Title: Sarcosine and other metabolites along the choline oxidation pathway in relation to prostate cancer--a large nested case-control study within the JANUS cohort in Norway.
studies.Reference: Sarcosine and other metabolites along the choline oxidation pathway in relation to prostate cancer--a large nested case-control study within the JANUS cohort in Norway.

extraction_supporting_text.cases: we conducted a nested case-control study among 3,000 prostate cancer cases and 3,000 controls
extraction_supporting_text.comparison: odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for prostate cancer risk were estimated according to quintiles of circulating betaine, dimethylglycine (DMG), sarcosine, glycine and serine

sample_size.excerpt: We included 6,528 men (24.4% African American) without a cancer diagnosis at baseline (1987-1989) followed through 2012.

cases.excerpt: Choline intake was not associated with total (n = 811) or lethal (n = 95) PCa risk overall or by race.

effect_size.excerpt: Betaine intake was inversely associated with lethal (tertile 3 vs 1, HR 0.59, 95% CI 0.35-1.00, p trend = 0.04), but not total PCa risk;

headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger’s test is generally not recommended when fewer than 10 studies are available.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 2 studies yielded an effect size of 1.01 (95% CI: 0.38–2.73), indicating no statistically significant association between betaine and prostate cancer. Although the point estimate suggests a potential positive relationship, the confidence interval includes the null. These findings were accompanied by very high heterogeneity (I² = 88.60%), reflecting highly inconsistent results across studies.
